artists.biography:
One of New York’s most notable ska bands, the Slackers formed in Brooklyn in 1991 and have played the world over many times since. Their first release was an eponymous self-released album, distributed by Moon Records in 1993 on cassette. Their first real debut is “Better Late Than Never” on moon ska records. Coming out in 1996, this album saw a movement to more traditional ska music, as opposed to their earlier two-tone and garage influences. It was produced by Victor Rice, a noted ska/reggae producer, who also played bass for them at one point.

Band members are as follows:
Vic Ruggiero - Keyboards, Vocals
Jay “Agent Jay” Nugent - Guitar
Dave Hillyard - Saxophone
Glen Pine - Trombone, Vocals
Marcus Geard - Bass
Ara Babajian - Drums

perplexity.description:
Don't Let The Sunlight Fool Ya," released in 2022 by The Slackers on Pirates Press Records, marks the band's first full-length album in six years. The record blends the group's signature mix of rock, reggae, and funk/soul, showcasing their ability to merge upbeat rhythms with introspective lyrics. The title track, written in the wake of the 2020 lockdown, sets the tone for an album that reflects on resilience and the deceptive comfort of returning to normalcy, all wrapped in the band's characteristic ska-infused sound.

Musically, the album features tight horn arrangements, soulful organ lines, and laid-back grooves that highlight The Slackers' seasoned musicianship. It stands as a strong addition to their extensive discography, reaffirming their status as stalwarts of the American ska scene. While not a commercial blockbuster, the album was well-received by fans and critics for its authenticity and timely themes, with outlets noting its relevance and the band's enduring ability to craft thoughtful, genre-blending music.
